trigger: an authenticated operator requests GET /api/v1/devices/{id} (and MCP get_agent_details) for an id OUTSIDE their management-group scope; the handler called lookup_device (a Postgres tag read on an existent hit) BEFORE the in_scope check
classification_rationale: the backing tag-read on an out-of-scope-existent id contradicted the #3564 not-found/out-of-scope indistinguishability invariant via a timing side-channel (the RESPONSE was already identical 404; only the DB round-trip leaked existence)
summary: #3564 residual timing oracle: out-of-scope /{id} + get_agent_details did a backing tag-read before the scope check, disclosing cross-scope existence by timing. Fixed by short-circuiting in_scope->404/denied BEFORE lookup_device in BOTH REST and MCP (byte-identical response, ZERO backing read). Independently reported by security-guardian and architect. Derives HIGH under strict rule-2 (I1 confinement leak + E3/E5); the two reviewers informally rated it MEDIUM. Fixed pre-push; new REST test asserts lookup_calls==0.

trigger: the served OpenAPI literal for GET /api/v1/devices/{id} said tags are 'omitted when no TagStore', but device_agent_detail_json emits tags unconditionally ([] when empty)
classification_rationale: the in-code served-doc literal contradicted the actual response shape
summary: Served OpenAPI literal corrected to 'tags always present, [] when empty'; tags?->tags[] in the response shape. Matches device_agent_detail_json.

trigger: the device page/info fragment showed 'Tags: none' for every device because get_one dropped DeviceDetail.tags when building DeviceRow
classification_rationale: the rendered 'none' contradicted the device's actual TagStore-sourced tags (capability shipped-incomplete/unreachable)
summary: get_one now populates d.tags from DeviceDetail.tags (key=value), restoring the single-device page/info Tags field. List path stays tagless by design.

trigger: the seam split the DEX/Guardian lenses into device_lens_routes.{hpp,cpp} but the device-pages routed-concern row did not name them, so a future change there routes no reviewers
classification_rationale: a required routed-concern trigger entry for a newly-created file was missing (a missing-required-doc absence, not a wording nit)
summary: device-pages row now names device_lens_routes.{hpp,cpp} / DeviceLensRoutes and the dex.device.view/guardian.device.view verbs.

trigger: the changelog fragment and matrix scope wording said 'the /devices dashboard search' although /devices redirects to /hardware; the affected surface is the legacy GET /fragments/devices/list fragment
classification_rationale: named the wrong (redirected-away) surface; gist correct but scope imprecise
summary: Changelog + matrix reworded to name /fragments/devices/list and note the /devices->/hardware redirect.

trigger: docs/user-manual/mcp.md get_agent_details entry did not state the now-firm tags-always-present contract
classification_rationale: required user-doc for the shipped tags-shape behaviour was absent
summary: mcp.md now states the tags array is always present ([] when none), mirroring the REST twin.

trigger: assorted low-value observations across the original pass (lens header include ordering; a redundant tag read on the page path; server.cpp member stop()-join ordering)
classification_rationale: cosmetic/defense-in-depth notes with no wrong outcome; grouped
summary: Reviewed the assorted NICE notes; no change required (cosmetic / defense-in-depth; the stop()-join ordering is safe as-is, the page-path read is not on a hot path).

trigger: MCP get_agent_details always emits tags (verified unconditional) but its typed OUTPUT schema listed tags outside required[], so an A5 machine-metadata consumer could not rely on presence from the schema alone
classification_rationale: the machine output schema under-promised vs the firm always-present behaviour (A5 wants machine metadata, not prose-only); direction-safe
summary: Added 'tags' to the get_agent_details output-schema required[]. Direction-safe (schema was under-promising).

trigger: two device_routes.cpp comments said 'tags always empty post-rewire', contradicting this seam's single-device page-path populate
classification_rationale: comment vs code (rule 3); functionally harmless as both sites are list-only, so native LOW
summary: Reworded both comments to scope the 'empty' claim to the list-only converter/predicate; the page/info path populates tags in get_one.

trigger: device_api.hpp #3564 banner said the consumer 'MUST check in_scope' but the dashboard consumer uses the ancestor-aware scoped_perm_fn, not flat in_scope
classification_rationale: over-specific verb; the deny-before-call invariant holds for all three consumers regardless, so no contradiction of behaviour
summary: Banner softened to 'apply its own confinement gate (flat in_scope for REST/MCP; ancestor-aware scoped_perm_fn for the dashboard) before calling'.

trigger: the tags-restore render path (get_one -> render_device_info_fragment) had no regression test, so a future refactor could silently revert to always-empty tags
classification_rationale: missing regression test for the headline fix (no present defect; regression-safety)
summary: Added a device_ui test: render_device_info_fragment renders key=value for populated tags and the 'none' placeholder when empty.

trigger: no MCP-side test mirrored the REST lookup_calls==0 assertion locking the #3564 short-circuit ordering
classification_rationale: missing symmetric regression test for the MCP short-circuit (no present defect; verified correct by reading)
summary: Added a lookup_calls counter to JsonDeviceApi, hoisted the harness handle, and asserted ZERO backing read across the out-of-scope get_agent_details call.

trigger: when device_api is unwired, MCP get_agent_details yields 'Agent not found' for an in-scope id while REST yields 503 'device registry unavailable'
classification_rationale: a pre-existing transport divergence (a global config fault, not per-id; fail-closed; no existence oracle); NOT introduced by this diff
summary: Pre-existing MCP-vs-REST divergence on the unwired-device_api path; left as-is (not introduced here, no security impact).
